items.longBusinessSummary: Applied Digital Corporation designs, develops, and operates digital infrastructure solutions to high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence industries in North America. It operates through: Data Center Hosting, and HPC Hosting Business. The company provides energized infrastructure services to crypto mining customers; and cloud services to customers, such as AI and machine learning developers. It also engages in the designing, constructing, and operating of data centers to provide computing power and support HPC applications. The company was formerly known as Applied Blockchain, Inc. and changed its name to Applied Digital Corporation in November 2022. Applied Digital Corporation is based in Dallas, Texas.

Title: TeraWulf Jumps 7% as CEO Pushes Back on Stranded Data Center Fears; Cipher Digital Rises 3%, Applied Digital Edges Higher
Author: David Moadel   Mon, October 26, 2026 at 4:56 PM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-10-26T15:56:04+00:00
=== BODY ===
Prager's "we don't build on spec" defense lifted WULF 7% and CIFR 3%, though TeraWulf still sits 26% below last month's levels.
WGMI climbed 3%, more than tripling SPY's 0.9% gain, as AI infrastructure stocks recovered alongside but outpaced the broader market.
TeraWulf backs Prager's no-spec claim with a contracted Anthropic lease at its Kentucky campus and a freshly expanded senior secured credit facility.
Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Cipher Digital didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat CIFR. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.
A weekend response from TeraWulf's (NASDAQ:WULF) chief executive is lifting the former Bitcoin miners now racing to build AI data centers, with TeraWulf shares leading the charge. The pushback targets a worry that has weighed on the group: some sites could end up without tenants, power or interconnection. TeraWulf shares are at $12.15 in morning trading, up 7% as the market reassesses fears that partially built data centers could leave computing capacity stranded.
Even with the rebound, TeraWulf stock is down 26% over the past month, so the gain recovers only part of that decline. Meanwhile, Cipher Digital (NASDAQ:CIFR) shares are up 3% to $8.17, a smaller advance that trails TeraWulf's move. Applied Digital (NASDAQ:APLD) shares are up 2% to $18.63, the most modest gain of the three data center builders.
The CoinShares Bitcoin Mining and Digital Power ETF (NASDAQ:WGMI) is up 3% to $30, giving a read on the sector. That's well ahead of the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY), which is up 0.9% to $767.08, showing the AI infrastructure group recovering alongside a stronger market while also outpacing it.
24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now. Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.
The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.
Over the weekend, TeraWulf chief executive Paul Prager pushed back on warnings that partially built data centers will leave computing capacity stranded. His case rests on sequencing, since TeraWulf secures power, fixed-price construction contracts, long-term tenants with investment-grade backing and financing before it builds. Prager wrote, "We may move dirt early, but we don't build on spec."
Prager made his stance clear. In the same pushback, he maintained that "what others call stranded assets, we may call a development pipeline." Late last week, TeraWulf also expanded its senior secured revolving credit facility, giving the company more borrowing capacity for its AI data center expansion. Taken together, the message and the larger credit line offer a concrete answer to the funding question hanging over TeraWulf's unfinished sites.
TeraWulf, Cipher Digital and Applied Digital all build data center capacity for AI and high-performance computing customers. Both TeraWulf and Cipher Digital are converting from Bitcoin mining, while Applied Digital built its business around hosting computing workloads. That shared origin puts TeraWulf and Cipher Digital in the same debate over how converted mining sites get financed and filled.
Contracted tenants anchor TeraWulf's argument, including a long-term Anthropic lease at its Justified Data Campus in Kentucky and existing operations at its Lake Mariner campus in New York. Prager's "development pipeline" line also covers earlier-stage TeraWulf sites such as the Muskie Data Campus in Kentucky and the Chesapeake Data Campus in Maryland. Cipher Digital has its own contracted campuses, including Black Pearl and Barber Lake, as it moves away from mining.
Applied Digital's hosting background gives it a different profile. The company runs an HPC Hosting segment serving hyperscale customers and a Data Center Hosting segment that provides energized space to crypto mining customers.
TeraWulf's next test is whether its financing-first approach keeps its projects on schedule amid broader questions about how AI data centers get funded (we covered seven companies supplying that expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report here). The milestones to watch are construction progress at Lake Mariner and Justified, along with any draw on the expanded credit facility.
On the risk side, TeraWulf still runs a legacy mining business it's repurposing for high-performance computing, and its sites take time to turn into lease revenue, while the expanded borrowing capacity at TeraWulf also adds obligations that pay off only if tenants move in on schedule.
Cipher Digital's contracted campuses support its case, but it faces the same conversion and financing questions, and Applied Digital's hyperscale customers are an advantage, though its crypto mining hosting segment keeps it tied to a volatile sector. Prager's no-spec pledge sets a clear standard for measuring TeraWulf in the quarters ahead.
If you have cash sitting in your account right now, give this two minutes. After more than two decades of helping investors beat the market, our top analysts at 24/7 Wall St. put together a definitive report on the Top 10 Stocks To Buy Today. And CIFR wasn't one of them.

Title: Musk says SpaceX closed $40 billion GPU debt deal, warns lenders are shutting out neoclouds
Author: William Foxley   Mon, October 26, 2026 at 3:17 PM GMT+1 2 min read
Published: 2026-10-26T14:17:31+00:00
=== BODY ===
SpaceX closed $40 billion of debt financing for GPUs, CEO Elon Musk said on X on Sunday. He credited the company's investment-grade standing and its Starlink and launch revenue for the access. In the same post, he warned that credit has dried up for operators without those advantages.
"As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers," Musk wrote. "That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many."
Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS), CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) and IREN (NASDAQ: IREN) traded lower before the open on Monday, according to Seeking Alpha. Benzinga said each was down more than 2% premarket. Applied Digital (NASDAQ: APLD) also came under selling pressure.
Stay ahead of AI infrastructure deals. Get Blockspace in your inbox.
In a follow-up reply, Musk said the deal is "primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter." CNBC reported on October 7 that banks and Apollo were discussing financing for a $40 billion Nvidia GPU purchase. A person familiar with the talks told CNBC that the deal would mainly tap the investment-grade market, likely with the GPUs as collateral.
SpaceX held $51.3 billion of cash and $38.6 billion of marketable securities at September 30. Against that, it carried $36.1 billion of long-term debt and finance leases. Management has guided fourth-quarter capex of $35 billion to $40 billion.
The neoclouds Musk targeted are already paying more for capital. CoreWeave's 9.75% senior notes due 2031 yielded 15.78% on October 15, and its five-year CDS spread topped 1,140 bps intraday, CNBC reported. On Thursday, Nebius announced a $3.5 billion senior secured loan from Citi. The loan has a 364-day maturity and is priced at Term SOFR plus 275 bps, with the margin able to step up to 350 bps.
IREN's $2.4 billion Blue Owl equipment financing for its Mackenzie campus carries a 9% rate and matures two and a half years after funding.
Nebius has pointed to its contract book as its next source of funding. "We still have a range of capital sources available to us to finance the next phase of growth, including asset-backed financing based on investment-grade customer commitments of more than $40 billion of long-term contracts," Chief Operating Officer Ophir Nave said in the Citi announcement.

Title: Applied Digital Keeps Cratering: This Analyst Keeps Insisting It’s Going to Jump by 390%
Author: Alex Sirois   Mon, October 26, 2026 at 3:45 PM GMT+1 6 min read
Published: 2026-10-26T14:45:17+00:00
=== BODY ===
APLD trades near its 52-week low after falling 33% in one month, yet 13 of 15 analysts rate it Buy or Strong Buy.
IREN and CIFR dropped 47% and 57% respectively in the same selloff, while APLD was the only one of the three beating estimates.
Applied Digital carries $6.4B in total debt and a -50% free cash flow yield despite holding a potential $86B contracted backlog.

Applied Digital (NASDAQ:APLD) currently trades at $18.25, while the average analyst target stands at $62.44. That gap implies 242.1% upside.
Applied Digital builds and runs purpose-built AI data center campuses in North Dakota and the southern U.S. It leases capacity to CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) and investment-grade hyperscalers and holds about $36B in contracted revenue. The highest target on the Street is more aggressive still. Lake Street Capital Markets analyst Rob Brown holds a $90.00 target, which works out to 393.2% upside. With a gap that wide, the market and the analysts disagree sharply on this stock.
Applied Digital has fallen 32.98% in one month. That is a selloff of more than 30%, and it started right after the strongest quarter in company history. Shares stood at $25.45 when the company reported fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $341.88M, beating the $124.57M consensus. Adjusted EPS of -$0.01 exceeded the -$0.3023 estimate, marking a 6th consecutive EPS beat.
SoFi Active Invest is offering a limited-time promotion. Open an account, fund it with $50 or more, and you could receive up to $1,000 in complimentary stock for Active Invest accounts. See for yourself by clicking here now. (Sponsor)
Investors looked past those beats to the balance sheet. The company posted a GAAP net loss of $184.06M and spent $2.07B on capex in the quarter. It has $6.4 billion in total debt against about $3.7 billion in cash and restricted cash. Rising yields and a sliding Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) price pressured the whole group. Rothschild & Co Redburn also initiated coverage at Neutral with a $22 target, highlighting execution, power and pipeline-conversion risks. As the stock hit a one-year low, co-founders Wes Cummins and Jason Zhang bought about $6.7 million in shares.
The contracted backlog supports the bullish thesis. Applied Digital has about 1.41 GW of leased critical IT load, and the contracts reach ~$86B if all renewal options exercised. Management expects "to place over 600 megawatts into service versus the 250 megawatts over the past 12 months."
Pricing is the next catalyst. Management expects about 250 megawatts of expansion leases by calendar year-end, with lease rates up "definitely north of 15%". The ChronoScale compute unit is on track for $1 billion of ARR in 2027. The longer-range target is 3.5 to 4 gigawatts by the end of calendar year 2030.
Recent analyst moves have mostly been reiterations and upgrades. Wells Fargo kept its Overweight rating and lifted its target to $55. Morgan Stanley stayed at Equal-Weight but upgrades its target to $41. Jones Trading initiated at Buy with a $70 target. Needham and B. Riley hold targets in the $70–$85 range.
The consensus fiscal 2028 EPS estimate has slipped to -0.7844 from -0.2500 30 days ago, which means analysts expect losses to continue for at least two more years.
The whole group sold off together, and Applied Digital held up better than its closest rivals.
IREN (NASDAQ:IREN) has dropped 47.07% in a month to $24.91. Its average target of $77.81 implies 212.4% upside, which is smaller than Applied Digital's. Of its 20 analysts, two call it a Strong Buy, 13 a Buy and five a Hold. Its latest quarterly revenue of $137.20 million missed estimates.
Cipher Digital (NASDAQ:CIFR) has fallen 56.73% in a month to $7.94. Its average target of $29.36 implies 269.8% upside, which is larger than Applied Digital's. Of its 22 analysts, five call it a Strong Buy, 15 a Buy and two a Hold, despite a Q2 EPS of -0.65 that missed estimates.
Cipher offers the biggest consensus upside among the three. Applied Digital has the most aggressive single target and is the only one of the three beating estimates. None of these targets is a guarantee.
At $18.25, Applied Digital trades near its 52-week low of $17.65 and far below its high of $50.73. The 15 covering analysts average $62.44, which implies 242.1% upside. The ratings break down this way:
The stock is down 25.57% so far this year, compared with an S&P 500 gain of 11.45%. Over one year, Applied Digital has lost 45.33%, against a 13.13% gain for the index. A beta of 6.0 explains why the moves in both directions are so large.
The bullish thesis improves if the 600-plus megawatts reach service on schedule and the expansion leases close at higher rates. Should both occur, base rent replaces one-time fit-out revenue and the 89% NOI margin on HPC operations starts to has the income statement. But the stock looks like a value trap if capital markets tighten before Polaris Forge 3 and the two Delta Forge campuses are financed. A free cash flow yield of -50.3% leaves little room for error.
The bullish thesis has support. The contracts are signed, insiders are buying, and Applied Digital is the only name in the group beating estimates. The $90 target needs years of flawless execution, so it reads as a ceiling, while the average target reflects a multiyear outlook. All of that AI data center expansion still has to be powered, cooled, and networked by somebody, and we rounded up seven suppliers doing exactly that in a free report on the AI boom beyond the chipmakers. Watch the stock around the next lease announcements.
